I am 63 this year, and I have worked this land in Quzhou since I was ten years old. I never went to school, but fifty-three years of waking up before dawn and watching the weather teaches you more than any book. My household has six people, and some of my children work off-farm in the city, so I do not have as many hands around as I used to. I must be smart with my 20 mu.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I double-crop wheat and maize on 15 mu because that rotation has never failed me. I keep 5 mu of cotton because the price is still decent, but I will not plant more than that—at my age, cotton is too much work with all the spraying, pruning, and pest watching it needs. I have a well, so water is not my biggest worry, but diesel and labor are.

For my wheat, I will use rotary tillage and sow an improved variety like the ones I have trusted for years. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and topdress with urea when the wheat greens up in spring. I will irrigate four times from my well—overwintering, green-up, jointing, and grain filling—if the skies do not do the work for me. I also spray two or three times for weeds and insects. I know this land, and I expect about 1000 jin per mu.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize the same day or the next. I use no-tillage for maize; there is no time to plow between crops, and the wheat stubble helps hold the moisture anyway. Maize is simpler to manage—two irrigations and a few pesticide sprays will carry it through. I should get around 1100 jin per mu if the summer storms do not flatten it.

For cotton, I will rotary till my 5 mu now in April and sow an improved variety. Cotton needs more care than the grains. I give it more fertilizer, especially potassium for the bolls. I will irrigate three times and spray for pests about fourteen times through the summer—the bollworm and aphids never rest around here. It is hard on my back, but 5 mu is just enough that I can handle it without hiring too much help. I expect about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu.

This is what I have always done, and this is what I will do this year. The land does not lie.
